headline: Failed Senate resolution would have required the President to remove U.S. troops from unauthorized hostilities with Iran.
what_it_does: This resolution would have directed the President to pull U.S. Armed Forces out of hostilities within or against Iran. The requirement would have applied unless Congress passed a declaration of war or an authorization to use military force against Iran. It would not have stopped the United States from defending itself, its personnel, or its facilities abroad from attack. On April 15, 2026, the Senate refused to take it up or end debate on it, so it did not pass.

who_it_affects.how: The President would have been required to end U.S. military involvement in hostilities against Iran unless Congress authorized it.
Troops taking part in hostilities within or against Iran would have been withdrawn from that fighting, though they could still defend against attacks.
Congress would have had to pass a declaration of war or a use-of-force authorization before such hostilities could continue.
